## Verdict: PASS — the failing line is fixed and no new blocker was found

## (1) The failing line of S1, re-run

| line | re-run (this round) | verdict | label |
|---|---|---|---|
| The bentcut report, and the committed summary's `t34.faces`, depend on `--workers`, against C-0242 (7) | **The fix.** In `index.ts`, the T34-1 phase still reads faces in batches of `max(10, 2·workers)`, but its inner loop now stops adding records once the n-th g has been drawn (`if (g.length >= sizes.t34) break;` before `t34Records.push`). The no-draws stop is a fixed face limit, `50 × n`, and the last batch is capped at `limit − j`. So `t34Records`, `t34.faces`, the phase's notes and the work block hold the faces in kind-round order up to the one that gives the n-th draw, whatever the batch size. **S1's own probe, re-run in the tree**: `bench -- bentcut --only t34 --t34 30` gives `(4 districts)` at `--workers 1` and also `(4 districts)` at `--workers 6`. The two reports, without `seconds`, are equal as JSON, and the work block has `districts` 4 / 4. S1 had 10 vs 12. **Default size, other batch sizes**: `bench -- bentcut --only t34` at `--workers 7` (batch 14) and at `--workers 2` (batch 10) both give `T34-1 mean of g over 10000 faces' draws (486 districts): 0.23327 … −0.03 s.e. — HOLDS`. The two reports are equal, and their t34 block is identical to the committed summary's. **The whole bar run in the tree at `--workers 4`** (S1's evidence run; the summary comes from the author's `--workers 6`): exit 0, `bars HOLD`, `T34-1 … (486 districts)`. `summaryOf(report)` from this run is **byte-identical** to `docs/build/summaries/M0-b-04.json` (`t34.faces` 486, work block `districts` 1500). S1 found 490 vs 492. **The pin**: `entry.test.ts` › *T34-1 does not depend on the worker count* runs `bentcut()` on an in-thread caching runner at 1, 6 and 7 workers and asserts equal reports. It also asserts that `t34.faces` and the work block's `districts` equal the face count it computes itself up to the 30th draw. **Negative control in the seat's mirror**: the fix's `break` line was deleted, so every face of every batch is kept again. The pin went red: `Test Files 1 failed (1)`, `Tests 1 failed \| 5 skipped (6)`, at `entry.test.ts:119` (`expect([w, await at(w)]).toEqual([w, one])`), with the work quantiles differing (`unitsTotal` 122 vs 227). The mirror was then restored, and `cmp` against the tree came back clean. **The one-time shift** (492 → 486) is recorded in C-0253 (3). The row also says that every other field is unchanged, and this run confirms that. | **fixed** | CONFIRMED |
